title: Ledger account activity event
description: The value of one record on the ledger.account-activity topic: what one account saw happen in one ledger entry. Derived from com.baran.ledger.domain.AccountActivityEvent under a snake_case naming strategy. The event id lives in the event-id record header, not here; see contracts/README.md.

transaction_id.description: public_id of the ledger transaction this entry belongs to. Two records of one transfer carry the same value; it is what a PSP settlement line echoes back.

account_id.description: public_id of the account posted to. Equals the record key, and is the only account attribute on the wire, so source mapping is by this value.

amount.description: Signed minor units (kurus). Negative on the account debited, positive on the account credited. The bounds mirror the amount_bounded CHECK and the exclusion of zero mirrors amount_nonzero.

currency.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic code of the account posted to. Structural only: which codes this service accepts is configuration, not part of the wire contract. The ledger is single-currency and emits TRY.

tx_type.description: The transaction type, as the producer's enum name. The producer emits TRANSFER, FUNDING and REVERSAL today; the ledger's valid_tx_type CHECK also admits FEE and ADJUSTMENT, and the ledger README states the contract may add further types. Open on purpose: a closed enum would dead-letter every event of a new type, and those events still move money on accounts this service reconciles. A value this service does not know is recognised but unmapped, not invalid; see docs/ledger-integration-notes.md section 5.5.

entry_id.description: id of the ledger_entries row this event describes, read back by the ledger's INSERT ... RETURNING. A reversal's events name the reversal's own entries, never the original's. This is the entry's identity in this service's projection; the event-id header stays the deduplication key. Optional, because events written before the field existed are still on the topic: absent is valid, present as null is not.

created_at.description: That entry's created_at column, in UTC with exactly six fractional digits, for example 2026-09-24T00:00:00.000000Z. When the ledger wrote the entry, not when the relay published it. value_date derives from it in Europe/Istanbul. Optional under the same rule as entry_id: absent is valid, present as null is not.

$comment: Unknown properties are allowed on purpose: the payload carries no schema version, so an additive ledger change would otherwise fail every event at once and take the projection down. A missing required field or a malformed known field still fails. entry_id and created_at are optional but come as a pair (dependentRequired): the ledger writes both or neither, so an event with one of them is drift. The pattern on created_at is structural; that the value is a real instant is checked when the consumer parses it.

uuid.$comment: A pattern rather than "format": "uuid", because format is an annotation in draft 2020-12 and only asserts when a validator is configured for it. The pattern fails the same input everywhere.
